Author response to Braillon: Practice guideline update summary: Mild cognitive impairment: Report of the guideline development, dissemination, and implementation subcommittee of the American Academy of Neurology
We have some concerns about the recommendations on cholinesterase inhibitors in the recent guidelines on mild cognitive impairment (MCI). [1] Evidence in the guidelines, and in systematic reviews, [2-4] clearly show that cholinesterase inhibitors have no reliable benefit on cognition and do not reduce progression to dementia.
The guideline panel thanks Valenzuela et al. for their thoughtful comments on the recommendations concerning the use of cholinesterase inhibitors for treating mild cognitive impairment (MCI). [1] The "may choose not" language resulted from the AAN guideline modified Delphi voting process.
